section: 14.2
title: The Character Table of $A_4$
---

The alternating group $A_4$ consists of the identity, the three double transpositions and the eight $3$-cycles. Its conjugacy classes are found with the splitting criterion for conjugacy classes in $A_n$ (Proposition [11.4.3](/notes/math-55a/11-4-conjugacy-in-s-n-and-a-n#proposition-11-4-3)): a conjugacy class of $S_n$ contained in $A_n$ remains a single conjugacy class of $A_n$ if some odd permutation commutes with one of its elements, and otherwise it splits into two classes of equal size. The transposition $(12)$ commutes with $(12)(34)$, so the double transpositions form one class of $A_4$. The centralizer of $(123)$ in $S_4$ has order $24/8 = 3$ (Proposition [3.2.13](/notes/math-55a/3-2-group-actions#proposition-3-2-13)), so it is $\langle(123)\rangle \subseteq A_4$, and the eight $3$-cycles split into the two classes $$\{(123),\ (134),\ (243),\ (142)\} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \{(132),\ (143),\ (234),\ (124)\}.$$ So $A_4$ has four conjugacy classes, and therefore four irreducible representations, the squares of whose dimensions add up to $12$.

*The $1$-dimensional representations.* The subgroup $K$ of Section [14.1](/notes/math-55a/14-1-the-character-table-of-s-4), consisting of $e$ and the three double transpositions, is a union of conjugacy classes, hence normal in $A_4$ (Proposition [3.2.13](/notes/math-55a/3-2-group-actions#proposition-3-2-13)), and $A_4/K$ has order $3$, so it is cyclic, generated by the coset of $(123)$. Every homomorphism $\theta : A_4 \to \CC^*$ is trivial on $K$: the three double transpositions are conjugate, so $\theta$ takes a common value $\varepsilon$ on them, with $\varepsilon^2 = 1$; and $(12)(34)\,(13)(24) = (14)(23)$ gives $\varepsilon^2 = \varepsilon$, so $\varepsilon = 1$. So $\theta$ factors through $A_4/K \cong \ZZ/3$, and with $\omega = e^{2\pi i/3}$ we obtain exactly three $1$-dimensional representations $U$, $U'$, $U''$, sending $(123)$ to $1$, $\omega$, $\omega^2$ respectively. (Here $U'$ and $U''$ are new; the alternating representation of $S_4$ becomes trivial on $A_4$.) Since $(132) = (123)^2$, their values on $(132)$ are $1$, $\omega^2$, $\omega$.

*The last representation.* The fourth irreducible representation has dimension $\sqrt{12 - 3} = 3$. The standard representation $V$ of $S_4$, with $A_4$ acting through the inclusion $A_4 \subset S_4$, has character $(3, -1, 0, 0)$ on $A_4$, and $$H(\chi_V, \chi_V) = \tfrac{1}{12}\bigl(9 + 3 \cdot 1\bigr) = 1,$$ so $V$ remains irreducible on $A_4$. It is the fourth irreducible representation.

:::note
The representation $W$ of $S_4$ does not stay irreducible on $A_4$. Its character on $A_4$ is $(2, 2, -1, -1)$, which equals $\chi_{U'} + \chi_{U''}$ because $\omega + \omega^2 = -1$; so on $A_4$, $W$ is isomorphic to $U' \oplus U''$. This also follows from the description of $W$ above: $K$ acts trivially, and $A_4/K$ maps onto the subgroup $A_3 \cong \ZZ/3$ of $S_3$, whose generator acts on the standard representation of $S_3$ with eigenvalues $\omega$ and $\omega^2$ (Lemma [13.3.4](/notes/math-55a/13-3-schurs-lemma#lemma-13-3-4)).
:::
